textInfo.description: The foundational revealed scripture of Kashmir Shaivism. 77 sūtras divided across three Unmeṣas, mapping precisely to the three great means of realization: Śāmbhavopāya, Śāktopāya, and Āṇavopāya.

verses.studyGloss: Consciousness is the Self.
verses.practicalContext: The foundational declaration: the true Self is living, sentient Consciousness (Caitanya), endowed with absolute freedom of knowledge and action.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Contracted, differentiated knowledge is bondage.
verses.practicalContext: Contracted, piecemeal knowledge that perceives division and separates the knower from the known constitutes the primary bond of Saṃsāra.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The matrix of differentiated sound and limited activity constitutes the body of ignorance.
verses.practicalContext: The illusion of separation is sustained by the groups of letters (phonemes) and limited functional capacities that shape the mental body.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The ununderstood mother of phonemes (Mātṛkā) is the ground of limited knowledge.
verses.practicalContext: The Sanskrit alphabet and inner verbal chatter unconsciously dictate psychological states, creating fear and longing.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The sudden surge of spontaneous spiritual exertion is Bhairava.
verses.practicalContext: The sudden, flashing upsurge of pure awareness before thoughts can crystallize is the direct embodiment of Bhairava.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through union with the wheel of energies, the differentiated universe is dissolved.
verses.practicalContext: When the seeker unites with the internal wheel of sensory powers, the illusion of external separate matter dissolves into light.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: In the distinctions between waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, the ecstatic expansion of the Fourth state (Turya) arises.
verses.practicalContext: Turya is not an isolated retreat; it is the living current that runs through and illuminates all three states of experience.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Waking is differentiated sensory cognition.
verses.practicalContext: For the bound person, waking is lost in external objects; for the yogi, waking is the radiance of Consciousness playing as external forms.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Dreaming consists of internal thought-constructs.
verses.practicalContext: Dreaming demonstrates how the mind constructs an entire universe of landscapes, people, and emotions purely out of mental impressions.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Lack of discernment is deep dreamless sleep immersed in Māyā.
verses.practicalContext: Ordinary deep sleep is enveloped in non-discernment; yogic sleep remains lucidly awake in the void.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The hero of spiritual awareness is the master and enjoyer of the three states.
verses.practicalContext: The realized practitioner (Vīra) does not flee waking, dreaming, or sleeping, but reigns over them as their master and enjoyer.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Astonished wonder is the stage and foundation of Yoga.
verses.practicalContext: Spiritual life is not grim ascetic suppression; it is a perpetual, joyful astonishment at the miracle of existence.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The sovereign Will of the realized master is the Goddess Umā, the ever-youthful Virgin.
verses.practicalContext: The will of an awakened master is identical to the pure divine creative energy of the supreme Goddess.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: All that is seen and experienced is one's own body.
verses.practicalContext: For the awakened yogi, the entire objective cosmos is experienced with the intimate immediacy of their own physical body.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through plunging the mind into the spiritual Heart, the objective world and void are perceived as one.
verses.practicalContext: Focusing the mind into the spiritual Heart dissolves the boundary between outer objects and inner silence.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Or through contemplation of the Pure Principle (Śiva), the uncontracted power of liberation arises.
verses.practicalContext: Attuning to the transcendental reality of Śiva frees the soul from the animal bonds of the Paśu state.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Unshakable conviction 'I am Śiva' is true knowledge of the Self.
verses.practicalContext: Vitarka here does not mean ordinary intellectual doubt, but the diamond-hard non-dual conviction: 'I am the Supreme Consciousness'.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The joy of observing the cosmos is the bliss of Samādhi.
verses.practicalContext: The yogi does not need to close their eyes to experience bliss; looking upon the world of people and nature yields the bliss of samādhi.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through union with Śakti, any body or state can be emanated at will.
verses.practicalContext: By aligning with the primordial creative energy, the master can project any experiential form at will.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: There is mastery over joining elements, separating elements, and synthesizing the cosmos.
verses.practicalContext: The fully awakened consciousness can unite and separate the elements of nature and perceive the cosmos in a single synthetic gaze.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through the dawn of Pure Knowledge (Śuddhavidyā), mastery over the wheel of all powers is achieved.
verses.practicalContext: When non-dual divine knowledge arises, the practitioner becomes the sovereign Cakreśvara.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through contemplation on the Great Ocean of Consciousness, the potent vitality of Mantra is directly experienced.
verses.practicalContext: By immersing in the boundless, transparent lake of Consciousness (Mahāhrada), the living potency of all mantras awakens.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The mind turned toward its source is Mantra.
verses.practicalContext: A mantra is not just a sound string; it is the mind deeply meditating on its non-dual identity with the Divine.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Spontaneous zealous effort is what accomplishes realization.
verses.practicalContext: Spiritual exertion in Śāktopāya is the eager, fervent turning of attention back toward the light of awareness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The secret of mantra is the being whose body is pure Knowledge.
verses.practicalContext: The true heart of all mantras is the living, radiant presence of the non-dual Goddess of Wisdom (Mālinī).

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Satisfaction with ordinary mental expansion is like dreaming of limited occult knowledge.
verses.practicalContext: The seeker must not be sidetracked by minor occult powers or visionary states, which remain within the dream of duality.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Upon the arising of Pure Wisdom, the innate state of Khecarī and Śiva is attained.
verses.practicalContext: When authentic intuitive wisdom awakens, one naturally enters the soaring flight in the sky of Consciousness (Khecarī).

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The Guru is the means.
verses.practicalContext: The Guru is the direct doorway to liberation, embodying the grace of Śiva that awakens the sleeping recognition in the disciple.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Awakening to the wheel of the Mother of Letters brings liberation.
verses.practicalContext: When the seeker decodes how language and letters construct psychological reality, the matrix of illusion is conquered.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The body is the sacrificial offering.
verses.practicalContext: In authentic tantric worship, one does not pour ghee into physical fire; one offers one's physical body and ego into the blazing fire of Consciousness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Differentiated knowledge is the food to be digested.
verses.practicalContext: All objective cognitions and perceptions are the nourishment that is chewed, digested, and integrated into pure Awareness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: With the fading of intuitive knowledge, dreamlike illusions emerge.
verses.practicalContext: If vigilance lapses and the light of pure wisdom is allowed to diminish, old dualistic impressions reassert themselves.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: For the bound soul, the fluctuating mind is mistaken for the Self.
verses.practicalContext: In the contracted state of Āṇavopāya, the individual identifies with the fluctuating mind (Citta).

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Sensory, fragmentary knowledge is bondage.
verses.practicalContext: Conditioned knowledge dependent on the senses keeps the soul trapped in dualistic perceptions.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Non-discernment of Kalā and the other tattvas is the illusion of Māyā.
verses.practicalContext: Failing to see that the five Kañcukas (Kalā, Vidyā, etc.) are only temporary coverings of one's own nature is Māyā.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: In the physical body, the parts and energies are to be reabsorbed.
verses.practicalContext: The practitioner methodically dissolves bodily energies from the gross elements up into the supreme center.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: There is mastery over the subtle channels, conquest of the elements, and discrimination from nature.
verses.practicalContext: Through breath regulation and subtle focus, one gains control over vital channels (nāḍīs) and physical forces.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Supernormal powers arise from the veil of delusion.
verses.practicalContext: Occult achievements are products of limited, veiled states and should not be confused with true liberation.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: By conquering delusion through infinite expansion, innate wisdom is won.
verses.practicalContext: Dissolving mental obscuration into boundless awareness establishes spontaneous natural wisdom (Sahaja-vidyā).

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Waking is a second radiant ray of awareness.
verses.practicalContext: For the dedicated yogi, ordinary waking reality is an illuminated ray of their own central consciousness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The Self is the cosmic dancer.
verses.practicalContext: The true Self dances through all situations and emotional roles on the stage of the cosmos without being tainted.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The inner soul is the stage.
verses.practicalContext: The subtle inner psyche provides the stage on which the cosmic dancer plays all parts.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The sensory organs are the spectators.
verses.practicalContext: The senses are the attentive audience watching the divine drama unfold.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through the purified intellect, the realization of pure Being is achieved.
verses.practicalContext: A clear, decisive intellect (Buddhi) becomes a perfect mirror for the light of pure consciousness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The state of sovereign freedom is established.
verses.practicalContext: The yogi achieves the unconditioned, autonomous nature (Svātantrya) of the Divine.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: As it is within one's own body, so it is everywhere else.
verses.practicalContext: The yogi realizes that the same consciousness vibrating within their heart is animating all living beings.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Constant mindful attention upon the primal Seed (Consciousness).
verses.practicalContext: Unbroken attentiveness directed toward the source of awareness preserves stability in daily life.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Established in the true posture, one effortlessly plunges into the lake of bliss.
verses.practicalContext: The true posture is resting effortlessly in Consciousness, plunging like a swimmer into a deep, cool mountain lake.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: One shapes external manifestations according to one's own measure.
verses.practicalContext: Consciousness shapes external experiences to mirror its inner state of realization.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: When spiritual wisdom is indestructible, the cycle of rebirth is destroyed.
verses.practicalContext: Continuous stabilization in non-dual recognition extinguishes all future rounds of conditioned rebirth.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The energies residing in the Ka-group of letters become the mother-powers of bound souls.
verses.practicalContext: The phonemic energies governing language control and entrap the bound creature until their divine origin is realized.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The Fourth state (Turya) is to be poured into the three states like a continuous stream of oil.
verses.practicalContext: One does not keep meditation separate from life; one infuses the peace of Turya smoothly into waking, dreaming, and sleeping.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Plunging with one's mind, one enters the inner sanctuary.
verses.practicalContext: By diving directly into the interior space of mind, one reaches the threshold of the transcendent.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through the harmonious flow of the vital breath, the vision of universal equality arises.
verses.practicalContext: When the inward breath (Prāṇa) and outward breath (Apāna) balance and rest in the center, equal vision (Sama-darśana) dawns.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: In the central state, inferior sensations are transcended.
verses.practicalContext: Resting in the central gap prevents the birth of lower reactive emotional turbulence.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through reuniting the objects of perception with the Self, what seemed lost is resurrected.
verses.practicalContext: When fragmented perceptions are reunited with awareness, the divinity of reality is restored.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: One becomes equal to Śiva.
verses.practicalContext: The practitioner realizes that they are in every respect identical to the Supreme Reality.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Every activity of the physical body becomes one's sacred vow.
verses.practicalContext: No external religious rituals are needed; walking, eating, breathing, and resting become sacred worship.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Ordinary conversation becomes the repetition of Mantra.
verses.practicalContext: Spoken words in daily life are experienced as the joyful vibration of the Great Mantra.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Bestowing knowledge of the Self is the highest charity.
verses.practicalContext: The greatest gift one can offer to humanity is awakening them to their own inherent divinity.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The master who presides over the wheel of powers is the cause of enlightenment.
verses.practicalContext: One who is firmly seated in sovereign awareness inspires awakening in everyone they touch.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The manifest cosmos is the boundless expansion of one's own energies.
verses.practicalContext: The universe is not an external prison; it is the glorious panorama of your own conscious powers.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Maintenance and dissolution also belong to the Self.
verses.practicalContext: The preservation and dissolution of experience are recognized as one's own voluntary rhythm.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Even while sensory activities proceed, there is no separation from the knower.
verses.practicalContext: Engaging in outward physical activities never disrupts the yogi's communion with the inner witness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Pleasure and pain are recognized as external phenomena.
verses.practicalContext: Pleasure and pain are seen as outer weather patterns that pass across the unchanging sky of the Self.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Freed from identification with them, one stands alone in absolute fullness.
verses.practicalContext: Detached from reactive emotions, the practitioner abides in the unconditioned sovereignty of Kaivalya.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Entangled in delusion, one becomes the bound agent of karma.
verses.practicalContext: Identifying with limited actions traps consciousness in the wheel of karmic consequence.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Upon overcoming the sense of difference, one gains the power to create anew.
verses.practicalContext: When division is dissolved, the yogi's actions carry the transformative creative force of the cosmos.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The creative power of the instruments arises from one's own direct experience.
verses.practicalContext: True power comes from direct personal realization, not secondhand theoretical concepts.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Infusing life from the primal state into the three spheres of being.
verses.practicalContext: Pouring the energy of pure consciousness into body, mind, and worldly actions.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Just as in the mind, so also in the body, senses, and external objects.
verses.practicalContext: The same spiritual stability maintained in internal contemplation extends seamlessly to the body and external world.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Due to craving, the bound soul is driven outward.
verses.practicalContext: Uncontrolled desire propels attention outward into the labyrinth of external objects.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Established in that awareness, with the end of craving, the bound state is dissolved.
verses.practicalContext: Abiding firmly in Consciousness, when craving ends, the contracted life of the limited soul dissolves.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.devanagari: भूतकञ्चुकी तदा विमुक्तो भूयः पतिसमः परः ॥ ३.४२ ॥
verses.iast: bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ || 3.42 ||
verses.studyGloss: Then, though still wearing the physical body as a cloak, one is liberated and identical to the Supreme Lord.
verses.practicalContext: Even while wearing the physical body like a lightweight coat, the realized master is in truth the supreme Lord Himself.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: The connection with vital breath is entirely natural.
verses.practicalContext: The ongoing biological breath continues naturally without obstructing transcendental awareness.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Through centering awareness in the inner space between breaths, what need is there for left, right, or central channels?
verses.practicalContext: When one rests directly in the inner center, external breath manipulations and channel techniques are naturally fulfilled.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.

verses.studyGloss: Again and again, there is the inward-and-outward blossoming of awareness.
verses.practicalContext: The enlightened life is a continuous, effortless dance of looking inward to pure silence and looking outward to divine play.

provenance.editionNotes: Canonical Devanagari text based on the Kashmiri recension with Kṣemarāja's commentary.
